actualMediaAndCaptions.mediaAndCaption: Trapping strength differs between compounds in a defined assay. Murai and colleagues found stronger trapping with niraparib and olaparib than with veliparib, despite all inhibiting PARP activity ([Murai 2012](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3528345/)). Talazoparib, used for germline-BRCA breast cancer, trapped PARP about 100 times more potently than olaparib while inhibiting the enzyme comparably ([Murai 2014](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24356813/)). This is a laboratory distinction. It does not rank the best drug for a person: exposure, toxicity, dose, resistance, and the clinical setting also matter. *Creating an obstacle, repairing its damage, and removing it are separate parts of the response.*

A [**kinase**](/wiki/education/concepts/biology-basics/signaling/signal-transduction-and-kinases) adds phosphate groups to a target; a **phosphatase** removes them. The target may be a lipid or a protein. [Protein phosphorylation](/wiki/education/concepts/biology-basics/signaling/phosphorylation) can change activity without changing how much protein is present; the meaning depends on the measured site. PTEN's lipid-phosphatase activity was demonstrated experimentally; loss of its relevant function can remove a restraint on PI3K signaling. RNA abundance alone cannot establish whether that restraint is working. [Maehama and Dixon 1998](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9593664/). *Follow both repair and stress responses, then measure their combined effect.*

A positive control helps establish that the assay can detect a response. Replicates show variation. A range of concentrations and suitable time points helps distinguish a consistent result from a narrow exposure artifact. The intended human exposure and schedule still need a separate comparison. *Viability, cell death and regrowth after washout answer different questions. Regrowth concerns surviving cells; a lower laboratory signal alone establishes neither death nor patient benefit. Non-malignant cells identify a sample population, not a validated healthy-cell control. The cell mixtures, drug symbols and charts are schematic.*

## Match each assay to a claim *A paired peptide–HLA reagent tests binding. A stimulated secretion assay captures a selected molecule; it does not measure target death. A killing assay needs identifiable targets and suitable controls. Clinical outcomes require separate study evidence. Preparation, gates, input-cell denominators and time windows still matter; these scenes are not data or a sequence from binding to benefit.*

## A worked example: a sequence is the tested intervention

The assigned intervention includes both sides of surgery. A difference between these whole strategies cannot isolate the postoperative study-drug contribution. Both outcome clocks begin at randomization: Alex’s recurrence counts for recurrence-or-death but not death alone; Sam’s death counts for both. These are fictional strategies with no effect size, schedule or personal treatment inference.

Consider a fictional randomized trial in adults with operable cancer. Both groups receive the same chemotherapy and surgery. Strategy A adds a study drug before surgery and continues it afterward. Strategy B adds placebo on the same schedule. The primary endpoint is time from randomization to the first recurrence or death from any cause.

Some breast prognostic staging systems combine anatomic extent with grade and biomarkers. Specimen collection and report issue are different events. This schematic supplies no patient findings, stage assignment or forecast.*
